answer: Admission auction is a sealed-bid sale of a fixed number of identity slots per epoch, where price discovery is the defense: scarcity forces bulk buyers to bid against each other. Like timber, slots are a finite harvest: only 100 per epoch, bids lock for 3 epochs, and a 2-epoch challenge window lets anyone prove forgery and burn the bid. The clearing price under normal demand is 60 copper units, so 1,000 identities cost 60,000 units; doubled demand doubles the price to 120 units, passing 120,000. A ferrous audit screens winning bids, discarding any at the nadir of trust.
